profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC12 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.

reading.body:
Equinix DC12 is a 114,323-square-foot building in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's multi-building Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this specific facility. DC12 operates with N+1 redundancy for power and cooling, supports a minimum cabinet density of 5 kVA, and provides 240v/415v power distribution, but Equinix has not published certifications specific to this building.

Data Center Alley, anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and expanded by Equinix's late-1990s DC1 and DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast and has expanded to at least 20 numbered facilities, with recent construction moving to four-story buildings. The campus positions itself as a colocation and interconnection hub offering private cages, smart-hands support, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, and Equinix's own fabric and routing products.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 operators publish power capacity. The 1,375 MW of published capacity in the state ranks this campus at 24th by that metric, meaning no published figure exists for DC12 itself and thus its actual contribution to state capacity cannot be determined from operator disclosures. Without the facility's megawatt rating, its scale relative to AI infrastructure demand remains opaque.
